source.title: Flatness-Aware Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics
source.authors: Stefano Bruno; Youngsik Hwang; Jaehyeon An; S. Sabanis; Dong-Young Lim

record.tranche_reason: Compares an adaptive optimizer with SGD on held-out image-classification accuracy using its own experiments, but does not reproduce the cited optimizer studies or their benchmarks.
record.gate_note: Only the AdamW-versus-SGD held-out accuracy comparisons bear on V4. The paper's fSGLD comparisons, Bayesian classification and OOD metrics, β–σ ablation, and Hessian-spectrum measurements do not test the listed claim versions. The text gives no training-accuracy results for the AdamW comparisons.
record.test_reason: The study's own SGD-with-momentum versus AdamW comparisons test V4 in noisy-label image classification and pretrained ViT fine-tuning. It uses 20 Optuna trials per optimizer, tuning learning rates and momentum or Adam coefficients, rather than the limited tuning in V4's main clause.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that fSGLD offers competitive or superior benchmark performance at comparable gradient-evaluation and memory cost, that the prescribed noise coupling is effective, and that Hessian measurements support its flatness mechanism. They also establish non-asymptotic convergence and excess-risk bounds for the Hessian-trace-regularized objective. They draw no specific AdamW-versus-SGD conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates a new flatness-aware SGLD optimizer on noisy-label benchmarks, with AdamW and SGD among broadly tuned baselines; it does not reproduce the original optimizer comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: AdamW-versus-SGD accuracy varies by architecture and training stage: AdamW trails in the scratch-trained ResNets but leads in ViT-B/16 fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.5 reports smaller maximum Hessian eigenvalues and Hessian trace for fSGLD than SGD and SGLD on selected ResNet-34 CIFAR-10N solutions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A flatness-aware optimizer can produce solutions with lower unscaled Hessian curvature. These measurements do not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap relationship.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The optimizer comparison uses noisy-label datasets; the AdamW and SGD comparisons report held-out accuracy but no training accuracy, so the study cannot establish whether any held-out difference accompanies equal or better training performance. Table 4 reports no uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for additional optimizer comparisons and the paper's fSGLD performance were left out because they do not bear directly on the listed versions. No claim-version result rows were otherwise omitted.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

The limited-tuning protocol; language benchmarks; equal or better training performance; adaptive optimizers other than AdamW; controlled changes in tuning breadth; isolated effects of decoupling weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD. Weight decay is fixed at different values for SGD and AdamW.
Batch-size comparisons and recipe adaptations under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, and interactions with augmentation or weight decay removal.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap rankings at similarly low training loss, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded accuracy values match Tables 3 and 4. Each SGD/AdamW row pair represents one comparison, not independent evidence. Small differences are marked partial without inferring statistical significance or absence from overlapping standard deviations. The tuning protocol does not isolate tuning breadth or weight-decay decoupling as causes of the observed differences.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Generalization as network width increases past interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance.

Language benchmarks; training-performance comparisons; decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD; comparisons with adaptive methods other than AdamW. The experiments use broad hyperparameter tuning, rather than only learning rates and decay schedules.
Large versus small batches and adaptations to batch-size training recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation tolerance and ranking against norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
